categories.title: Core goals
categories.intro: Seven default control loops for most long-running brownfield work.

categories.title: Specialist goals
categories.intro: Six distinct loops for incidents, upgrades, migrations, branch recovery, optimization, and feasibility.

categories.title: Product and quality goals
categories.intro: Nine focused loops for frontend, documentation, security, reliability, APIs, operations, developer experience, data quality, and audit readiness.

goals.title: Brownfield Continue / Finish
goals.simple: Understand the real current state and keep completing the most important unblocked work.
goals.use_when: An existing repository has an approved direction, partial implementation, or unfinished milestone and should advance autonomously.

goals.title: PRD / Spec Compliance
goals.simple: Compare the real product with its requirements and close every proven gap.
goals.use_when: A product, feature, or repository must be brought into full alignment with documented requirements.

goals.title: Next Milestone
goals.simple: Deliver one useful next milestone without wandering into the whole backlog.
goals.use_when: A roadmap is larger than one run and the next coherent, dependency-safe increment should be completed end to end.

goals.title: Deep Audit + Remediation
goals.simple: Find important problems, prove they are real, fix root causes, and prevent recurrence.
goals.use_when: The codebase needs evidence-based discovery and repair of important defects or risks.

goals.title: QA / Regression / UAT
goals.simple: Exercise the real product until required workflows and regression gates pass.
goals.use_when: The actual product surface and realistic user workflows must pass defined acceptance gates.

goals.title: Safe Refactor / Modernization
goals.simple: Improve internals while proving users and integrations still see the intended behavior.
goals.use_when: Architecture, dependencies, or internals should change while external behavior and contracts remain stable.

goals.title: Release Readiness
goals.simple: Remove verified release blockers and stop at release-ready.
goals.use_when: A version or milestone must satisfy all release gates without actually being published or deployed.

goals.title: Incident Recovery / Stabilization
goals.simple: Contain damage, restore health, prove the cause, and add prevention.
goals.use_when: A severe regression or production-like incident must be contained, diagnosed, and recovered without compounding damage.

goals.title: Dependency / Framework Upgrade
goals.simple: Upgrade through safe version steps while checking the full compatibility surface.
goals.use_when: A dependency, framework, language runtime, or toolchain must move to a target version without breaking supported behavior.

goals.title: Data Migration / Integrity
goals.simple: Migrate data through reversible phases and prove no unexplained loss, duplication, or corruption.
goals.use_when: Stored data, schemas, formats, or backfills must change while preserving correctness, compatibility, and recoverability.

goals.title: Branch Rescue / Integration
goals.simple: Recover useful behavioral slices without overwriting newer target work.
goals.use_when: Valuable work is stranded in a stale, divergent, oversized, or conflicting branch and must be recovered safely.

goals.title: Measured Optimization / Benchmark
goals.simple: Freeze a baseline, test one challenger at a time, and keep only reproducible wins.
goals.use_when: A stable metric must improve under a fixed protocol without regressing required behavior.

goals.title: Technical Spike / Feasibility
goals.simple: Run an isolated experiment and return a Go, Conditional Go, or No-Go decision.
goals.use_when: A bounded technical unknown must be resolved before production commitment.

goals.title: Frontend UI / UX / Accessibility
goals.simple: Improve the real interface through browser-based user journeys, visual evidence, and accessibility checks.
goals.use_when: A frontend surface must become coherent, usable, responsive, accessible, and visually polished without regressing behavior.

goals.title: Documentation Synchronization / Knowledge Transfer
goals.simple: Find documentation drift, verify examples and commands, and make the maintained knowledge trustworthy.
goals.use_when: Documentation, examples, runbooks, diagrams, or onboarding material must accurately match current behavior and be usable by its audience.

goals.title: Security / Privacy Hardening
goals.simple: Threat-model the scoped system, prove actionable findings, remediate safely, and add lasting protection.
goals.use_when: Security and privacy are the primary outcome: attack surface, authorization, secrets, dependencies, or data handling must be hardened and verified.

goals.title: Reliability / Resilience Hardening
goals.simple: Model failure modes, inject safe faults, improve recovery, and prove reliability objectives.
goals.use_when: A system must continue or recover correctly under defined failures, load, retries, restarts, and dependency degradation.

goals.title: API / Integration Contract Compatibility
goals.simple: Map contracts and consumers, prove compatibility, and evolve interfaces without hidden breakage.
goals.use_when: APIs, events, schemas, SDKs, or external integrations must remain compatible across producers, consumers, and versions.

goals.title: Observability / Operability
goals.simple: Make system health visible and actionable, then prove it with drills.
goals.use_when: Operators and maintainers must be able to detect, understand, and recover from important failures using useful signals and runbooks.

goals.title: Developer Experience / Tooling
goals.simple: Make the common developer path work from clean state with clear commands and actionable failures.
goals.use_when: Local setup, build, test, debug, CI, or contribution workflows must become faster, clearer, and reproducible.

goals.title: Data Quality / Pipeline Assurance
goals.simple: Define data invariants, test the real pipeline, correct root causes, and make quality continuously observable.
goals.use_when: A data pipeline or dataset must satisfy defined freshness, completeness, validity, consistency, lineage, and reconciliation expectations.

goals.title: Compliance / Audit Readiness
goals.simple: Map controls to implementation and evidence, close technical gaps, and leave an auditable package for qualified human review.
goals.use_when: A repository or system must produce implementation evidence for an approved control set without falsely self-certifying legal or regulatory compliance.
